pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p1: A circuit linking the cool microclimate of El Crucero with the Pacific coast at Pochomil. Includes transport, guided tour, lodging, meals and sun-and-beach activities.
pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p2: Historical and cultural circuit: Historic Center, Tiscapa Hill, Old Cathedral, Central Park, National Palace of Culture, Paseo Xolotlán and Puerto Salvador Allende.
pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p3: A 45-minute night walk along El Cráter Trail. Watch nocturnal wildlife, the Mombacho salamander, sleeping birds, bioluminescent insects and illuminated views of Granada.
pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p4: Historical and river immersion: the Fortress of the Immaculate Conception, the colonial history of Rafaela Herrera, the riverside village of El Castillo and tropical nature on the river.
pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p5: Adventure expedition in the northern mountain range with the local team Zipote Vago Tours. Cliffs, mountain hiking, natural pools and traditional Segovian food.
pages.experiencias.expPkgCard.p6: Pristine coral islets in the Caribbean Sea. Departure from Pearl Lagoon, safe boat transport with life jackets, coral reef, Creole breakfast, Caribbean lunch and kayaks.

pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p1: Connecting the Great Lake Cocibolca with the Caribbean through four great navigation routes, living history, biodiversity and life alongside the Rama indigenous people.
pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p2: The legendary interoceanic gold-rush route of the 19th century: Managua → San Juan del Sur → Río San Juan → El Castillo → Greytown → Indio Maíz Reserve.
pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p3: Spanish colonial trade, riverside fortifications and the saga of the Desaguadero. Includes the Fortress of the Immaculate Conception, museums and the village of El Castillo.
pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p4: Birdwatching in the wetlands of San Carlos, San Miguelito, Solentiname and Los Guatuzos Refuge. Herons, kingfishers, roseate spoonbills and red-lored parrots.
pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p5: Exploring the Indio Maíz and Bartola biological reserves. Primary rainforest, caimans, howler monkeys, manatees and ancient ceiba trees with baqueanos.
pages.experiencias.rutasRioSanJuan.p6: Community lodging and direct homestays with families of the Rama indigenous people. Tours guided by ancestral leaders through columnar basalt formations, medicinal hot springs and pristine trails.

pages.miNegocio.faqList.div1: Does Baqueano charge any commission on my sales?
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div10: Payment is 100% direct: the explorer coordinates with you by WhatsApp, email or phone, and pays however you both prefer (cash, transfer, bank deposit). Baqueano shows your direct contact on your profile. There is no intermediary payment gateway. Integration with Tilopay/BAC will soon be available for those who want it, but always optional and without Baqueano commissions.
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div11: Can I update my business information later?
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div12: Yes. Once your registration is approved, you'll get access to a management portal where you can update prices, schedules, photos and availability. Changes go through a quick review by the Administrator (usually less than 24 hours) before appearing in the app and on the website.
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div2: No. The Baqueano model is designed to eliminate financial intermediation. The explorer pays your cooperative or business directly. Baqueano facilitates the connection but does not touch or retain any percentage of your income. This is what we call "tourism with rural sovereignty".
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div3: Do I need INTUR registration to join?
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div4: It is not a strict requirement to sign up, but it is highly recommended. INTUR registration gives you access to the incentive regime of Laws No. 1210 and 1211, which promote community tourism development. The Baqueano team can guide you through INTUR registration if you need it.
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div5: How long until my business appears in the app?
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div6: Once your request is sent, the General Administrator reviews it in the Ops Center within 48-72 business hours. If the information is correct and verifiable, your business is published on the web map and in the Android app. You'll receive a confirmation email with your official host badge.
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div7: What is the trail GPS beacon system?
pages.miNegocio.faqList.div8: GPS beacons are satellite safety points that baqueano guides activate in the Android app when starting a tour. Explorers and their emergency contacts can see the location in real time. If an incident occurs, the SOS feature sends exact coordinates to emergency numbers and to the Baqueano Desk's WhatsApp.

pages.miNegocio.legalFrameworkSection.h2: Tourism Laws No. 1210 and 1211 & INTUR Categories
pages.miNegocio.legalFrameworkSection.li: Direct coordination between INTUR and local and regional governments.
Formal recognition of service providers in communities.
Protection and preservation of the nation's natural and cultural heritage.
Exemptions on capital goods and tourism construction materials.
Direct support for formalizing SMEs and rural cooperatives.
Accreditation of quality and environmental sustainability standards.
pages.miNegocio.legalFrameworkSection.p1: Tourism development in Nicaragua rests on the current legal framework promoted by INTUR and the National Assembly, guaranteeing tax incentives for local businesses and recognizing 13 official categories of tourism activity.
pages.miNegocio.legalFrameworkSection.p2: It sets the guiding principles of sustainability, competitiveness and sovereignty of Nicaraguan tourism. Article 16 defines and classifies the official tourism categories that energize territories and promote community inclusion.
pages.miNegocio.legalFrameworkSection.p3: Law on Incentives for Tourism Development (updated 2026). It provides tax benefits, tax exemptions and investment facilities for lodging, restaurant, tourist transport and ecotourism projects.
